_note: The shape a device-reading threshold rule would take, with no threshold in it. Named directly by packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json's device tier and its refusal device-threshold-carries-no-number-until-ratified: 'A device-class allowlist entry (packages/catalog/devices/thresholds.json) carries no numeric threshold until a ratified entry here names it. Until then the class exists with no threshold, and a reading against it is recorded but never auto-creates an incident.' This file is that entry as it stands today: the reading types and device classes a threshold could someday apply to, and the rule that gates one, with the thresholds array itself empty.
_populatedNote: THIS FILE HOLDS NO LIVE NUMERIC THRESHOLD. The thresholds array below is empty and stays empty until a clinical-review-queue.json entry reaches state ratified with tier "device" and names a specific reading type and device class. scripts/check-boundaries.mjs (not touched by this change) is the intended enforcement point for that rule; this file only states it. Anybody populating a row in the thresholds array without a ratifiedEntryRef pointing at a ratified queue entry is doing exactly what the queue's refusal exists to prevent.
_governedByWhy: Reuses the queue's existing device tier rather than inventing a second gate. The queue's own tiersNote already says scripts/check-boundaries.mjs 'fails the build if a device-class allowlist entry (packages/catalog/devices/thresholds.json, once it exists) carries a number with no ratified entry here naming it' — this file is the 'once it exists' the queue was written ahead of, and it exists now holding nothing.

readingTypesFrom.why: A threshold is a rule about a reading type, and records.json already owns every reading type MyThuso records and the unit each is recorded in (packages/catalog/devices.json metrics already reuses this same source rather than retyping a measure list). This file does not restate that list; a threshold row, once one exists, names a measure by the id records.json gives it.

deviceClassesFrom.why: certified, consumer, simulator — devices.json's own three classes, and the only ones any reading is ever registered under. A threshold row, once one exists, names one of these three, or the device tier this catalog's packages/catalog/devices/pairing-paths.json proposes as a finer distinction within them; it never invents a fourth class of its own.
deviceClassesFrom.consumerNeverThresholded: A threshold naming deviceClass consumer would be meaningless before it is even ratified: packages/catalog/devices.json's clinicalWeight already ensures a consumer reading never carries clinical weight and is never published on reading.ingested@1, so there is no event for any threshold rule to ever act on. This file states that plainly rather than leaving a reader to work out why a consumer row would never appear.

ruleShape._note: What a threshold row would hold once one is ratified. Documented as a shape, not populated, so a later generator or boundary check has something to target without any of it being live today.

fields.why: This rule's own reference, once one exists.
A measure id from packages/catalog/records.json#observations.measures. Required; a threshold with no reading type names nothing.
certified or the medical-grade tiers packages/catalog/devices/pairing-paths.json names within it. Never consumer, per consumerNeverThresholded above.

Whether the rule fires above, below, or outside a range — the shape of the comparison, not the number, so the shape itself can be reviewed by the clinical governance board ahead of any number being proposed.
The number itself. Always null in this file and in any entry that is not live — see boundValueAlwaysNull below.

Restated as its own field, deliberately redundant with the nullable annotation above, because a generator that only checks a JSON Schema's nullable flag could still be handed a non-null number by a careless edit; a human or a script reading this file sees the constraint twice before it could ever be missed once.

What firing the rule does once it is live — today the only value this file describes is 'record only,' matching the queue's own words that 'a reading against it is recorded but never auto-creates an incident' until ratification. Any stronger action (auto-creating an incident) is exactly what the queue's device tier exists to gate, and this field never carries one until a ratified entry says so.

A reference into packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json naming the entry, at state ratified, tier device, that authorised this specific rule. Required on every row that is not empty; a row with no ratified entry to point at is not a row this file may hold, per the queue's own refusal.
Who proposed it, mirroring the queue entry's own proposedByRef so the two records agree on authorship rather than each keeping a separate copy.

_thresholdsEmptyWhy: Zero rows, on purpose, today. Nothing in packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json has ever reached state ratified — its own preview says so: 'No entry has ever been proposed. This file describes a queue with nobody in it.' A thresholds array with rows in it while the queue has never ratified anything would be this file breaking the exact discipline it exists to hold.

refusals.statement: No row is added to thresholds until a clinical-review-queue.json entry naming it reaches state ratified.
refusals.why: Restates packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json's own device-threshold-carries-no-number-until-ratified refusal from this file's side, so a reader who opens thresholds.json first, without having read the queue, still sees the rule that governs it rather than an empty array with no stated reason.
refusals.answeredByWhy: No route reads or writes this file today — no device threshold route exists anywhere in packages/catalog/apis/devices.json. This refusal is enforced, when it is enforced, by scripts/check-boundaries.mjs against the queue, which this task does not touch; it is stated here for whoever writes that check, not claimed as already firing.

refusals.statement: A threshold never names deviceClass consumer.
refusals.why: See deviceClassesFrom.consumerNeverThresholded above: a consumer reading never reaches the event bus a threshold rule would act on, so a rule naming it would be dead on arrival, and dead rules invite someone to wire a second, unaccountable path for a consumer reading to matter clinically.
refusals.answeredByWhy: Same as above — enforcement is scripts/check-boundaries.mjs's, once written.

preview: No device class carries a numeric threshold. No reading against any device today auto-creates an incident, and this file's whole purpose is to keep that true until a named clinician's name, role and day appear in a ratified entry saying otherwise.
